name: Venetium (Windows RT)
author: hamed7ir
description: Venetium is Chromium 150 (150.0.7871.226) for old ARM Windows tablets. This is the thumb2 build for the original Windows RT 8.0 and 8.1, on the Surface RT (Tegra 3) and Surface 2 (Tegra 4). Windows RT only runs Thumb-2 code, so I ported V8, the JavaScript engine of Chromium, to Thumb-2, and the JIT is on. It's built on Supermium and ungoogled Chromium, and it's a PGO and ThinLTO build. I tested it on my Surface RT with Windows RT 8.1: pages, scrolling and video work, and the sandbox is on. Telegram Web and Discord work too, and so does casting to a TV. Since 1.4, sites with very big WebAssembly don't stop the tab anymore, but some JetStream tests still run out of memory on RT 8.1. RT 8.0 should work, but I haven't tested it on a device yet, and there it draws in software, because RT 8.0 has no Direct3D shader compiler. Qualcomm devices like the Lumia 2520 no longer crash at start, but they still need testers. It has a built-in ad and tracker blocker (EasyList and EasyPrivacy) that is on by default. On Windows 10 build 15035, use the normal ARM32 build, Venetium. It's faster there.
instructionSteps: On Windows RT, jailbreak the device first. RT only runs unsigned desktop apps after a jailbreak.
Run Venetium-Setup-150.0.7871.226-win8-8.1-arm32-thumb2.exe. It installs for your user only, with shortcuts and an uninstaller, and doesn't need admin.
The files are not signed, so SmartScreen warns the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.
Upgrading from an older version: close Venetium, then install 1.4 over it.

In the setup you can choose the icon: Venetium, a flat WinRT style one, the logo of Venetium for Windows 10 Mobile, or your own .ico. To change it later, close Venetium and run set-icon.exe in the Venetium folder.
The ad and tracker blocker is on by default. To allow a site, use the "ads blocked" icon in the address bar, or turn the blocker off in chrome://settings/content/ads.

Once a week Venetium checks GitHub for a newer release and shows a bar under the toolbar with a download link. It never downloads or installs anything by itself. To turn it off, start Venetium with --disable-venetium-update-check.
If a video stops playing, start Venetium with --disable-features=VenetiumArm32CodecSteering and tell me the site.
